solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chap recalled skill: something frequently repeated

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: called back, so the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A fellow remembers a talent of his, something he keeps coming back to.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted over and over in meditation, hence any slogan constantly reiterated.

clue.text: Fellow got older and coped

parts.note: a fellow is a man
aged means grew older

explanation.surface: A man grew old and dealt with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have managed is to have got by or dealt with difficulty, a synonym of coped.

clue.text: Chip in spinach omelette

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words spinach omelette, across the gap

explanation.surface: A crisp found inside an egg dish with greens.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served with cheese and salsa.

clue.text: Be an efficient controller of this unit: graph organised

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters of this unit and graph are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A manager's chart is in order, showing the unit is well led.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a tight ship is an idiom for managing an organisation strictly and efficiently.

clue.text: Effect of legislation introduced by one politician

indicators.note: the law comes after, as if presented by, the one politician who brings it in

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
MP is Member of Parliament
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A single MP brings in a new law and it has some effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact as a noun is the influence or consequence something has, a synonym of effect.

clue.text: Rampaging mobs hesitated and lost an opportunity

indicators.note: running wild, so the letters of mobs and hesitated are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Rioting crowds dithered and let their chance slip by.
explanation.definitionFit: Missed the boat is an idiom for having been too slow to take a chance.

clue.text: Pardon sailor to work things out

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
to solve is to work out puzzles or problems

explanation.surface: Forgiving a seaman so he can sort out his problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to release someone from guilt or blame, as a pardon does.

clue.text: Proved trustworthy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tested, put on trial

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one claim that someone has shown they can be relied on; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tried is both a past tense of try, to test, and an adjective for something already proven dependable.

clue.text: I'm unable to comply with prisoner being sent back with nothing

indicators.note: returned, so the slang word for the prisoner is written backwards

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
and means together with
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A refusal to cooperate when a convict is returned to jail empty-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal phrase of refusal, saying the request cannot be carried out.

clue.text: Squeal, having zero stuff to write with

parts.note: O resembles zero
ink is what a pen writes with

explanation.surface: A cry of complaint at having no ink left.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting squeal made by a pig.

clue.text: Japanese food coming with S American greeting

parts.note: taken as the letter S, from the clue's S American
US, United States, abbreviates American
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Japanese cuisine arrives along with a South American hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'S American' looks like South American, but the S stands alone and 'American' gives US.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, a staple of the cuisine of Japan.

clue.text: Spirit of good army

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: The morale of a fine body of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is the spirit of a dead person, a synonym in the supernatural sense.

clue.text: Annoyed born Democrat was ahead of things

parts.note: née, born, introduces a maiden name
D abbreviates Democrat in US politics
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: A natural Democrat is irritated at being out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To be needled is to be provoked or irritated, a synonym of annoyed.

clue.text: Get off sled, as it were, in heavy rainfall?

parts.note: the prefix de- means off or away from, as in derail or detrain
a luge is a small racing sled

explanation.surface: Dismounting from a sledge in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As it were' and the question mark admit the playful split: de-luge would mean getting off the luge, just as detrain means leaving a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a flood or torrential downpour, an extreme heavy rainfall.

clue.text: New joke penned in the toilet back in the day

indicators.note: enclosed, so the joke and the new letter sit within the toilet word

parts.note: loo is British slang for the toilet
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A fresh joke written in the lavatory in years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned' suggests writing graffiti but means enclosed; loo is British for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Long ago means in the distant past, the same idea as the idiom back in the day.

clue.text: Hasten to change capital

indicators.note: the letters of the word hasten are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An urge to make a quick move to a different city.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, an example of a capital.

clue.text: Belted out revolutionary song making wine drink

parts.note: to belt out a tune is to sing it loudly, so sang

indicators.note: turning round, so the word for the song is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Someone sang a rebel song loudly while making a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine with fruit.

clue.text: Starts to shred packaging after receiving box

indicators.note: the beginnings of the four words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: Ripping open the wrapping after taking delivery of a carton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like the parcel being received, but it is the definition and the verb; the initials come from four words, not two.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box, especially in practice bouts.

clue.text: Football player with reward for waiting? Fancy shoe

parts.note: a wing is a player on the flank of a football side
a tip is money given to a waiter, a reward for waiting at table

explanation.surface: A footballer gets a bonus for his patience, and buys smart footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waiting' suggests patience but means serving at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingtip is a brogue-style shoe with a decorated toecap shaped like a bird's wing.

clue.text: Covers hip-hop songs on the radio

indicators.note: broadcast, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: raps are hip-hop songs

explanation.surface: A DJ plays cover versions of rap tracks on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' tempts as cover versions of songs, but it means wraps up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wraps as a verb means envelops or covers something up.

clue.text: Mischievous and somewhat self-involved

indicators.note: only part of the word self-involved, its middle stretch, is taken

explanation.surface: A description of someone both naughty and a bit egotistical.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin can mean impish, playful like an elf, hence mischievous.

clue.text: Fount damaged mattress

indicators.note: broken, so the letters of fount are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fountain has spoilt a mattress with water.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a thin Japanese-style mattress laid on the floor or on a frame.

clue.text: Embarrass a party

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: Showing someone up at a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted, a synonym of embarrass.

clue.text: Toreros carved up bird

indicators.note: cut into pieces and reassembled, so the bullfighters' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bullfighters slice up a fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male domestic chicken, a cockerel, so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Busybodies getting silverware returned

indicators.note: sent back, so the word for the cutlery is read backwards

parts.note: spoons are silverware, cutlery

explanation.surface: Nosy people get the cutlery handed back to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Snoops are people who pry into others' affairs, the same as nosy busybodies.

clue.text: Maybe Laurel's recited a piece of poetry

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: Stan Laurel of Laurel and Hardy is a possible Stan, so Stan's, said aloud with a z sound

explanation.surface: Perhaps the comedian Laurel performs some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy; 'Stan's a' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.
